battle.name: 西班牙再征服墨西哥
battle.theater: 墨西哥南部伊瓜拉至瓦哈卡走廊
battle.brief: 一八二一年一月，西班牙殖民當局調兵南下，企圖平定格雷羅在瓦哈卡與格雷羅兩省的游擊，把新西班牙的內地重新收復；遠征軍二月在奇納梅卡受挫，戰局最終以《科爾多瓦條約》與獨立法案收場。長槍這時已退出野戰序列，只在民兵長矛與營制條令中留形。

kit.name: 長槍
kit.history: 方陣的長矛讓火槍隊站在後面。密西西比之後，長矛和火槍一起站住了。

countries: 西班牙一方是新西班牙總督區的殖民政府與它的軍隊。攝政總督胡安·德·奧多紐胡於一八二一年七月抵達墨西哥城，接手一個已被十一年消耗戰掏空的殖民政府；他的下屬包括總督區的正規營伍、由本地市民與農民拼湊而成的民兵「志願兵」，以及散在各省城鎮與傳教站的守備分遣隊。指揮分兩條線：北線是若阿金·阿雷東多率領的北方軍，藉海路運兵、逐點收復科阿韋拉、新萊昂與坦皮斯科；南線是維森特·菲洛梅納·卡德納與何塞·瑪麗亞·梅爾卡多率領的遠征軍，專責追打格雷羅的游擊隊。南方遠征軍只帶走數千人，砲與輜重靠騾隊輸送，縱隊一旦斷了給養，戰力便要打折。墨西哥一方沒有統一指揮，三股力量並存：南部以維森特·格雷羅為首的土生游擊隊，靠鄉里關係與地形作戰；阿古斯丁·伊圖爾維德於同年二月組成的「三保障軍」，起點不過是原皇家陸軍第七營改編的數百人；以及各地自行其是的省級軍隊與義勇民兵。英國與美國當時都不承認墨西哥獨立，西班牙自由派與費爾南多七世復辟派之間的角力，也直接決定了這一年是談判還是硬打的分岔。
countriesEn: The Spanish side was the colonial government of the Viceroyalty of New Spain and its armed forces. Juan de O'Donojú, the interim viceroy appointed by the liberal government in Madrid, reached Mexico City in July 1821 and took over a colonial administration hollowed out by eleven years of destructive war. Under him stood the regular regiments of the viceroyalty, a militia of voluntarios made up of local townsmen and peasants, and small garrison detachments scattered through provincial capitals and mission stations. Command ran on two fronts. The northern front was the army of the North under Joaquín de Arredondo, who moved troops by sea and recovered Coahuila, Nuevo León and Tamaulipas point by point. The southern front was the expedition of Vicente Filomena de la Cadena and José María Mercado, whose task was to hunt down Guerrero's guerrillas; it took only a few thousand men into the field, with guns and baggage moved by mule train, so that a column cut off from supply lost much of its fighting power. The Mexican side had no unified command: three forces ran in parallel. First the indigenous guerrilla bands of the south led by Vicente Guerrero, who fought on local networks and on terrain; second the Army of the Three Guarantees that Agustín de Iturbide raised in February of that year, which began as a few hundred men reassigned from the former royal line regiment; third provincial troops and armed volunteers who took orders from nobody. Neither Britain nor the United States recognised Mexican independence at the time, and the struggle between the liberal government in Spain and the restored absolutism of Ferdinand VII decided whether the year ended in negotiation or in renewed fighting.
people: 這場戰爭的關鍵人物，一半在山區的游擊隊裡，一半在馬德里與墨西哥城。米格爾·伊達爾戈神父一八一〇年在瓜納華托的多洛雷斯起事，點燃十一年戰火；他的接班人何塞·瑪麗亞·莫雷洛斯一八一五年在奇瓦瓦被槍決，獨立運動的第一個高潮就此中斷。維森特·格雷羅是南部的實際統帥，他用小部隊、夜襲與游擊把皇家派遠征軍拖在瓦哈卡與格雷羅的山區，一八二一年二月二十二日於奇納梅卡打敗卡德納的遠征軍；三月他與伊圖爾維德會師，同年秋被任命為新生的墨西哥共和國首任總統，兩年後被解除兵權，於一八二九年在奇利潘辛戈附近遇刺身亡。阿古斯丁·伊圖爾維德是另一條線的關鍵人物，他以帝制傾向與教會立場拉起三保障軍，二月二十四日於奇爾潘辛戈公布三保障計畫，同年八月二十四日與總督奧多紐胡在科爾多瓦簽訂條約，其後成為墨西哥皇帝。攝政總督奧多紐胡是自由派任命的官員，他到任後選擇承認既成事實，而不是再打一場一五二一年那樣的征服戰。北線的阿雷東多代表殖民軍的強硬路線，靠海路與據點封鎖收復東北三省。卡德納與梅爾卡多指揮南方遠征軍，卻在奇納梅卡受挫；兩人的經歷說明一八二一年的癥結——殖民軍的戰術機器仍然完整，缺的只是能配合它的政治決心。
peopleEn: The key figures in this war were split between the guerrilla bands of the mountains and the counting houses of Madrid and Mexico City. Miguel Hidalgo, the priest who raised the revolt of 1810 at Dolores in Guanajuato, lit the fuse of eleven years of war; his successor José María Morelos was shot in Chihuahua in 1815, and the first great surge of the independence movement ended there. Vicente Guerrero was the real commander in the south: he kept the royalist expedition pinned in the mountains of Oaxaca and Guerrero with small columns, night attacks and ambushes, and on 22 February 1821 defeated Cadena's expedition at Chinameca. In March he joined Iturbide, and in the autumn of that year he was named the first president of the new Mexican republic; two years later he was stripped of his troops and was killed in the neighbourhood of Chilpancingo in 1829. Agustín de Iturbide was the key figure on the other line. He raised the Army of the Three Guarantees on a legitimist and ecclesiastical platform, proclaimed the Three Guarantees at Chilpancingo on 24 February, and signed the Treaty of Córdoba with the viceroy O'Donojú on 24 August of the same year, before becoming emperor of Mexico. The interim viceroy O'Donojú was an appointee of the liberal government, and on arrival he chose to accept what had already happened rather than to attempt another conquest of the kind Cortés had carried out in 1521. Arredondo on the northern front represented the hard line of the colonial army, recovering the three northeastern provinces through the sea route and a chain of blockhouses. Cadena and Mercado commanded the expedition in the south and were checked at Chinameca; their careers show where the pinch was in 1821 — the colonial war machine was still intact, and what it lacked was a political decision to use it.
kits: 這張卡的兵器是長槍。十六世紀的西班牙方陣由長矛與火槍兩種兵組成，標準大方陣三千人裡約一千五百名長矛兵、一千五百名火槍手，分成兩個各含五百人的分隊小方陣，長矛在前擋住騎兵與散兵，火槍手在後輪流射擊。科爾特斯一五二一年攻特諾奇蒂特蘭用的正是這個組合，長槍因此成為西班牙海外戰爭最鮮明的標記。但到了一八二一年，長槍早已不在野戰序列上：滑膛燧發槍配上刺刀才是這一年步兵線的骨幹。西班牙殖民軍留下的長槍痕跡只剩兩種，一種在編制上：首都與各省仍設有持長柄斧的長槍兵營，以及以長矛為主的志願兵騎槍隊，這些單位的任務與十六世紀長矛手完全一樣，在正面擋住對方騎兵，掩護後排裝填；另一種在條令上：殖民步兵操典仍以分隊小方陣與縱隊為核心，線列射擊、縱隊行進、結方陣自保的動作全都承自火槍與長矛並存的年代。南部游擊隊用的是短卡賓槍、馬刀與長矛，攻擊多在夜裡與峽谷中進行；皇家派遠征軍除燧發滑膛槍外，還有六磅、八磅野戰砲與臼砲，砲車用騾子牽引，糧秣靠牛車與騾隊輸送。值得留意的是，雙方「前排用長柄兵器頂住」的習慣並沒有消失，消失的只是武器本身。
kitsEn: The weapon on this card is the pike. The sixteenth-century Spanish tercio was built from two kinds of soldier, pike and shot, and in a standard full tercio of three thousand men about fifteen hundred carried pikes and fifteen hundred muskets, drawn up in two sub-squadrons of five hundred each, the pike in front to absorb cavalry and loose troops while the musketeers fired in rotation behind. That combination was exactly what Cortés used against Tenochtitlan in 1521, and the pike consequently became the most conspicuous badge of Spain's wars overseas. By 1821, however, the pike was long gone from the order of battle: the smoothbore flintlock musket with its bayonet was the backbone of the infantry line in that year. Only two traces of the pike survived in the Spanish colonial army. One was organisational: the capital and the provinces still raised companies of halberdiers, as well as lancer units of the volunteers whose long spears were meant for exactly the work the sixteenth-century pikemen did — holding the front against enemy horse and covering the reload of the men behind. The other was doctrinal: the colonial infantry manuals still taught the sub-squadron and the column, and the motions of line firing, column movement and forming square all came down from the age when pike and musket stood together. The southern guerrillas carried short carbines, machetes and lances, and attacked mostly at night and out of ravines; the royalist expedition carried flintlock muskets, field guns of six and eight pounds and a few howitzers, the guns towed by mules and the food and fodder moved by ox carts and mule trains. It is worth noticing that neither side lost the habit of holding the front with polearms; what disappeared was the weapon, not the practice.
tactics: 一八二一年的對抗有兩種戰術節奏。其一是皇家派的系統性收復：主力集中到省會周圍，設立封鎖線與據點驛站，逐年把游擊隊從要道擠向邊地，配上地方民兵分隊清剿；北線阿雷東多把海路與陸路平行推進，用船隻把部隊直接送過障礙較少的海岸，再以連鎖據點切斷游擊隊與山區的聯繫，終於在蒙特雷一線把新萊昂的游擊壓平。遠征南方時，卡德納與梅爾卡多採取正面推進加殲滅戰，想把格雷羅從山區趕進河谷。其二是格雷羅的游擊戰法：不與遠征軍在開闊地交鋒，專打補給線、側翼與落單分隊，在奇納梅卡選擇有利地形反擊，人數劣勢靠突然性與地勢抵銷，回擊之後立刻分散脫離。第三是天候與道路的節奏：六月至九月雨季，大軍難以在山區展開，衝突退化成小隊遭遇；旱季才出得起遠征。南北幹線順著山脈與河谷鋪開，騾隊一天走數十公里，遠征軍一旦斷了給養，縱隊就會拖成散兵線。最後，決定結局的不是會戰而是談判：南方戰事在軍力上無法收束，奧多紐胡於八月二十四日在科爾多瓦用條約換取西班牙撤軍，獨立隨即由政治手段完成。
tacticsEn: Two tactical rhythms run through 1821. The first was the systematic reconquest of the royalists: the main body was concentrated around the provincial capitals, a cordon and a chain of garrison posts were established, and the guerrillas were squeezed year by year from the main roads back towards the frontier, with local militia detachments doing the mopping up. On the northern front Arredondo advanced by sea and by land in parallel, using ships to move troops past the least obstructed stretch of coast and then chaining posts together to cut the guerrillas off from the mountains, until the rising in Nuevo León was flattened around Monterrey. In the south Cadena and Mercado tried the method of deliberate advance and decisive battle, hoping to push Guerrero out of the hills into the river valleys. The second was Guerrero's way of war: he would not meet the expedition in the open, but struck at its supply lines, its flanks and any detached column, and at Chinameca chose ground where a counter-stroke could be made, cancelling the disadvantage in numbers with surprise and terrain and dispersing again at once. The third rhythm was that of weather and road: in the rains from June to September no army could deploy in the mountains and the fighting degenerated into small meetings of detachments, and only in the dry season could a column get far. The trunk roads north and south ran along the ranges and the river valleys, a mule train covered only a few tens of kilometres a day, and once supply was cut the expedition column stretched into a straggling line. What settled the outcome was not a battle but a negotiation: the southern war could not be closed by force, so on 24 August O'Donojú used the Treaty of Córdoba to buy the Spanish withdrawal, and independence was finished by political means.
data: 關鍵日期排列得很密。一八一〇年九月十六日，多洛雷斯在瓜納華托起事；到一八二一年九月為止，獨立戰爭打了十一年。一八二一年一月，南方遠征軍自墨西哥城出發；二月二十二日奇納梅卡之戰，二月二十四日伊圖爾維德在奇爾潘辛戈公布三保障計畫，三月一日在伊瓜拉重申；三月裡阿雷東多進入蒙特雷，新萊昂的收復完成；八月二十四日簽訂科爾多瓦條約；九月十四日奧多紐胡進入墨西哥城；九月二十七日獨立法案在舊總督府通過，九月二十八日簽署生效。距離上，墨西哥城到普埃布拉約一百三十公里，奇爾潘辛戈約三百公里，瓦哈卡與格雷羅之間的山地驛道全靠騾隊，單頭騡子的負重約八十至一百公斤。兵力上，遠征軍以數千人計，格雷羅的游擊隊只有數百人，至多不過千人上下，雙方差距極大；新西班牙的皇家軍在紙面上有數萬人，但真正能作戰的正規營伍遠少於此，多數是民兵與守備。武器上，十六世紀大方陣的比例是三千人中一千五百長矛兵對一千五百火槍手；到一八二一年，燧發滑膛槍每分鐘可發二至四發，有效射程一百五十至三百公尺，刺刀成為前排唯一屏障，砲兵則是六磅與八磅野戰砲、少量臼砲。
dataEn: The key dates crowd close together. On 16 September 1810 Dolores raised the revolt in Guanajuato, and the war of independence ran for eleven years to September 1821. In January 1821 the southern expedition left Mexico City; the battle of Chinameca was fought on 22 February; on 24 February Iturbide proclaimed the Three Guarantees at Chilpancingo and repeated them at Iguala on 1 March; in March Arredondo entered Monterrey and the recovery of Nuevo León was complete; the Treaty of Córdoba was signed on 24 August; O'Donojú entered Mexico City on 14 September; the Act of Independence passed in the old viceroyal palace on 27 September and was signed on the 28th. As to distance, Mexico City lies about 130 kilometres from Puebla and about 300 from Chilpancingo, and the mountain tracks between Oaxaca and Guerrero were carried entirely by mule, one animal taking roughly eighty to a hundred kilograms. In strength, the expedition numbered some thousands against Guerrero's several hundred, at most around a thousand — a very wide gap. The royal army of New Spain numbered tens of thousands on paper, but the regular battalions actually fit to fight were far fewer, most of the force being militia and garrison. As to weapons, the sixteenth-century tercio was balanced at fifteen hundred pikes against fifteen hundred muskets in three thousand men; by 1821 a flintlock smoothbore musket fired two to four rounds a minute at a useful range of 150 to 300 metres, the bayonet was the only shield the front rank had, and the artillery consisted of six- and eight-pounder field guns with a few howitzers.
cause: 要理解一八二一年為何會打成收復戰，就得回到一八一〇年的起事根源。波旁王朝的財政與教區改革把礦區與鄉村逼到飢荒邊緣，一八〇八年的王位更替與半島戰爭又抽走了稅源與物資，軍隊在城外鎮壓，於是多洛雷斯在瓜納華托喊出號召，十一年戰火由此燒遍南北。一八一〇至一八二一年這場戰爭的實質，是西班牙王國能否靠常備軍重新控制新西班牙。十一年的消耗下來，皇家派在北線連勝：科阿韋拉、一八一九年收復的坦皮斯科、一八二一年三月平定的新萊昂，讓殖民當局相信剩下的只是幾股散兵，只要集中兵力就能連根拔起。於是有了南方遠征軍，有了北線的據點封鎖，也有了「收復」這個說法本身。但一八二一年還疊著一層變數：馬德里正在自由派三年期與費爾南多七世的復辟之間換班，前者派奧多紐胡來談，後者則由軍方與殖民當局要打。攝政總督、殖民軍將領、馬德里中央政府三方各懷算盤，遠征軍在最需要全速推進時收到的卻是一連串限制令。遠征南方之所以拖成持久戰，技術上是因為格雷羅的游擊隊避戰加上雨季，戰略上是因為殖民當局始終不肯承認政治解決，結果一場純粹的收復戰爭，被拖成了新國家的催生。
causeEn: To understand why 1821 turned into a war of reconquest, one has to go back to the roots of the revolt of 1810. Bourbon fiscal and ecclesiastical reform drove the mining districts and the countryside to the edge of famine, and the change of sovereign in 1808 and the Peninsular War drained away revenue and supplies; the troops stationed in the towns did the pressing, and so Dolores gave the signal in Guanajuato, and eleven years of fire burned from north to south. The substance of the war of 1810 to 1821 was whether the crown could reassert control of New Spain with a standing army. After eleven years of attrition the royalists kept winning on the northern front — Coahuila, Tamaulipas recovered in 1819, Nuevo León settled in March 1821 — and the colonial authorities came to believe that what remained was only a handful of bands, to be mopped up by a concentration of force. Hence the expedition into the south, hence the blockhouse line in the north, hence the very word reconquest. But 1821 carried a further complication: Madrid was changing hands between the liberal Trienio and the restored Ferdinand VII, the former sending O'Donojú to negotiate and the latter backing the army and the colonial authorities to fight. The viceroy, the colonial generals and the central government in Madrid each pursued their own account, and the expedition received a string of restrictions at the very moment it needed to move fastest. The southern campaign became a war of attrition for reasons of technique — Guerrero's guerrillas avoided battle and the rains did the rest — and of strategy, because the colonial authorities never would concede a political solution. A war of pure reconquest was thus dragged out until it gave birth to a new state.
impact: 一八二一年九月的結果，是三百年的西班牙統治在墨西哥終結。新西班牙總督區自一五三五年的設置到一八二一年被新生的墨西哥共和國取代，這條時間線的終點正是這場收復戰爭的失敗。科爾多瓦條約的領土條款留下一條很長的尾巴：墨西哥同意放棄得克薩斯、新墨西哥與上加州，作為西班牙協助收復這些地區的交換；條約從未落實，因為西班牙並沒有能力越過美墨邊界把地盤拿回來，而這些被放棄的地方，後來成了美國與墨西哥糾紛的源頭，也成了西班牙一八二九年自古巴再組遠征軍時手裡的藉口。軍事的後果同樣具體：南方游擊隊在勝利之後被收編，格雷羅交出兵權、一八二九年遇刺身亡，格雷羅州與瓦哈卡的鄉村武裝從此被拆散；新軍以三保障軍改編皇家軍而來，軍紀與財政都談不上，國家在沒有戰事的年份裡度過了最虛弱的開局。最後是武器與操典的傳遞：火槍與長矛並存的方陣理論，連同分隊小方陣、縱隊與結方陣的動作，一起被新軍的操典接收；長柄斧兵與長矛騎兵也作為儀仗與民兵裝備留了下來。三保障軍在編制上把舊體制的軍人與新國家的象徵捏在一起，這也成了此後半個世紀墨西哥軍隊的特徵。
impactEn: The outcome of September 1821 was the end of three centuries of Spanish rule in Mexico. From the establishment of the viceroyalty of New Spain in 1535 to its replacement by the new Mexican republic in 1821, that long line of time ends precisely at the failure of this war of reconquest. The territorial clause of the Treaty of Córdoba left a very long tail: Mexico agreed to cede Texas, New Mexico and Upper California in exchange for Spanish assistance in recovering them. The clause was never carried out, because Spain had no capacity to push past the new Mexican border to take the land back, and the territories given up were later to become the source of the quarrel between the United States and Mexico and the pretext Spain would use when it tried to mount another expedition from Cuba in 1829. The military consequences are equally concrete: the southern guerrilla bands were incorporated after their victory, Guerrero surrendered his troops and was killed in 1829, and the armed bands of Guerrero state and of the Oaxacan villages were broken up. The new army was the old royal army reorganised as the Army of the Three Guarantees, with neither discipline nor revenue, and the country passed its weakest opening years without a war to fight. Last comes the transmission of arms and drill: the doctrine of the tercio, in which pike and musket stood together, together with the motions of the sub-squadron, the column and the square, was taken over into the manuals of the new army, and halberdiers and lancers survived as ceremonial troops and as militia equipment. The Army of the Three Guarantees fused the men of the old order with the symbols of the new state, and that fusion became a feature of the Mexican army for the next half century.
result: 以軍力收復墨西哥的目標落空。一八二一年一月的南方遠征軍出發時指望一季之內解決南部，二月二十二日奇納梅卡一戰就宣告失敗；北線雖然成功收復三省，卻只證明可以拿下幾個省城，無法消滅遍布鄉村的武裝。到八月，戰爭實際上已由軍事轉為談判：八月二十四日奧多紐胡在科爾多瓦與伊圖爾維德簽訂條約，承認墨西哥獨立，換取西班牙軍隊有秩序撤出；九月十四日奧多紐胡進入墨西哥城；九月二十七日獨立法案在舊總督府通過，九月二十八日簽署，墨西哥共和國宣告成立。戰爭的結果因此是雙重的：對西班牙而言，收復失敗，帝國在美洲的解體自墨西哥開始，之後是聖多明各、委內瑞拉與秘魯的戰役，最後在一八二四年玻利瓦爾於胡寧與博伊西卡戰役之後，整個西班牙美洲帝國不再存在；對墨西哥而言，獨立以一場未完成的收復戰爭為代價而來，戰勝者不是任何一支軍隊，而是談判。西班牙直到一八三六年才正式承認墨西哥獨立，條約中那條收復北方的承諾，此後再沒有軍隊把它兌現。
resultEn: The attempt to reconquer Mexico by force failed. The southern expedition that set out in January 1821 expected to settle the south within a season, and the battle of Chinameca on 22 February ended that expectation at once. The northern successes in recovering three provinces showed only that provincial capitals could be taken, not that the bands scattered through the countryside could be destroyed. By August the war had in practice shifted from operations to negotiation: on 24 August O'Donojú signed the Treaty of Córdoba with Iturbide, recognised Mexican independence, and obtained an orderly Spanish withdrawal; on 14 September O'Donojú entered Mexico City; the Act of Independence passed in the old viceroyal palace on 27 September and was signed on the 28th, and the Mexican republic was proclaimed. The result was therefore twofold. For Spain the reconquest failed, and the dissolution of the empire in the Americas began with Mexico, followed by the campaigns in Santo Domingo, Venezuela and Peru, until after the battles of Junín and Boyacá in 1824 the Spanish American empire no longer existed. For Mexico, independence had been bought at the price of an unfinished war of reconquest, and the victor was no army at all but a negotiation. Spain did not formally recognise Mexican independence until 1836, and the promise in the treaty to recover the northern provinces was never carried out by any army.
